Our Initial Quick Thoughts on Autopilot Recall 


CITI’S TAKE 

Please see below for our initial thoughts on the Tesla Autopilot recall: 


Tesla is recalling vehicles >2mln vehicles for an Autopilot-related issue. The issue will 
be remedied via an over-the-air (OTA) software update, so we’d expect the recall to 
have a de minimis impact in terms of costs. 


At first glance, it appears that the intended remedy is mainly through the addition of 
extra alerts/cues, checks while using the feature outside of highways and when 
approaching traffic controls and a simplification of engagement – all in effort to make 
sure Autopilot is used in accordance with its intended use cases. 

That said, there was one part of the remedy that could be viewed as incrementally 
restrictive – a suspension for improper use if the driver repeatedly fails to drive 
responsibly. Our initial view here is that we believe this could be seen as a negative for 
customer experience, but ultimately the impact will depend on some variables, 
including: 1) the duration of the suspension; and 2) the number of those involved in 
the recall that currently use the system improperly.

Tesla Inc 

Valuation 


Our approach is to use a probability weighted Bull vs. Bear terminal value analysis. We construct a Bull case, a Base case and a 
Bear case. Our Base case is DCF-driven based on our earnings model (assumes 34x terminal 2030E adj. EBITDA and 12% 
discount rate), while our Bear and Bull cases draw downside/upside scenarios. Our target price then ascribes probabilities to 
each scenario. Our current price target assigns 20%/75%/5% weightings, respectively, to these three scenarios—yielding a 
$255 blended stock outcome. 


Risks 


This stock is High Risk based on our quantitative model, but we do not apply a High Risk rating due to Tesla’s improved financial 
performance and stronger balance sheet (positive FCF + capital raise). 
Potential upside risks to our price target include: 


If we began seeing signs that demand is consistent with the LT bull case narrative; 
If Tesla’s margin performance (ex. credits) experienced a meaningful and sustainable expansion beyond our estimates, then 
that would be supportive of a lasting competitive advantage; 


New product announcements related to Car of the Future (Cybertruck, Semi); 
If remaining/recent legal investigations turn out more favorably. 
If the impact from the above risks turns out to be greater than we anticipate, the shares could exceed our target price. 
Potential downside risks to our price target include: 
Macro & competitive pressures putting pressure on ASPs and gross margins; 
Supply-chain related disruptions could impede volume growth and/or lead to margin inefficiencies; 
The potential for adverse legal and/or regulatory developments; 
Execution risk with expanded capacity and new product rollout.

Catalyst Watch Upside/Downside calls: 


Citi Research may also include a Catalyst Watch Upside or Downside call to highlight specific near-term catalysts or events 
impacting the company or the market that are expected to influence the share price over a specified period of 30 or 90 days. A 
Catalyst Watch Upside (Downside) call indicates that the analyst expects the share price to rise (fall) in absolute terms over the 
specified period. A Catalyst Watch Upside/Downside call will automatically expire at the end of the specified 30/90 day period 
(or earlier if the investment rating of the company is assigned Rating Suspended or Under Review status); the analyst may also 
close a Catalyst Watch call prior to the end of the specified period in a published research note. A Catalyst Watch Upside or 
Downside call may be different from and does not affect a stock's fundamental equity rating, which reflects a longer-term total 
absolute return expectation. For purposes of FINRA ratings[1]distribution-disclosure rules, a Catalyst Watch Upside call 
corresponds to a buy recommendation and a Catalyst Watch Downside call corresponds to a sell recommendation. Any stock 
not assigned to a Catalyst Watch Upside or Catalyst Watch Downside call is considered Catalyst Watch Non-Rated (CWNR). 
For purposes of FINRA ratings-distribution-disclosure rules, we correspond CWNR to Hold in our ratings distribution table for 
our Catalyst Watch Upside/Downside rating system. However, we reiterate that we do not consider CWNR to be a 
recommendation. For all Catalyst Watch Upside/Downside calls, risk exists that the catalyst(s) and associated share-price 
movement will not materialize as expected.
